findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false through misleading logic
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` reads the `sqlExpressions` feature flag, negates it into a variable named `enabled`, and then returns `false` on both branches. The flag lookup has no effect, and the name and structure suggest the toggle still controls the feature when it does not. A future maintainer could "fix" the inverted-looking logic and silently re-enable the vulnerable path. Replace it with an explicit, commented hard-disable (e.g. `return false // disabled due to CVE-2024-9264`), or remove the helper and return the error directly in the `QueryTypeSQL` case.

findings.title: Misleading error returned even when the feature flag is enabled
findings.body: The `QueryTypeSQL` case returns "sqlExpressions is not implemented" for every request, including from users who explicitly turned on the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle. That wording reads like a missing build or feature rather than a deliberate security disable, which will cause confusion and support load. Use a clearer message, e.g. "SQL expressions are disabled", and consider logging or deprecating the flag.

findings.title: Existing parser/SQL command tests will now fail
findings.body: `TablesList` now uses the stub `NewInMemoryDB()`, whose `RunCommands` always returns "not implemented". `NewSQLCommand` and `Execute` likewise always fail. Any existing tests that assert table extraction or SQL execution results (e.g. `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go`, `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go`, SQL cases in the expr reader/service tests) will now fail. None of them are updated or skipped in this PR, so the change will likely break CI, or leave tests that silently assert on behaviour that no longer exists.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path bypasses the new gate and fails with an opaque error
findings.body: The new disable check lives only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. `UnmarshalSQLCommand`, used by the rawNode/legacy pipeline, still calls `NewSQLCommand`. That call now fails inside the `TablesList` stub, so users get a generic "error reading SQL command" BadRequest instead of a clear "SQL expressions are disabled" message. The protection is not applied in one central place, so a future change to the stub could re-open this path. Put the disable check in `NewSQLCommand` or `UnmarshalSQLCommand` as well.

findings.title: Injection-prone SQL construction left in place behind a stub
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` by string formatting user input, with only single-quote doubling as protection. This pattern is the attack surface behind the CVE. It is now inert only because the stub DB always errors. Anyone who later swaps a real engine back into `NewInMemoryDB` would immediately reintroduce the vulnerable code path. Remove the dead SQL-building code, or clearly mark it as unsafe.
